clue.text: Disappointed no end having received a bronze — diabolical

indicators.note: the trimmed word takes the following pieces into its middle, as if receiving them
the final letter of the synonym is dropped, leaving it endless

parts.note: sick, as in 'sick as a parrot', means thoroughly disappointed
a bronze is a suntan, so tan

explanation.surface: Someone disappointed at a third-place medal reacts in a fiendish way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disappointed' as 'sick' is British slang ('sick as a parrot'); 'no end' drops its final letter and 'having received' takes the bronze inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic and diabolical are synonyms, both describing devilish wickedness.

clue.text: Filming British playboy in old estate car

parts.note: shooting a film is filming
a rake is a dissolute playboy

explanation.surface: A British womaniser is filmed driving a vintage station wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: A shooting brake is the old British name for an estate car, a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: The term once meant a vehicle for carrying shooting parties, later a station wagon.

clue.text: Short film associated with a queen

indicators.note: the film's name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Titanic is the 1997 blockbuster film

explanation.surface: A brief movie about a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims TITANIC to TITANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Relative with board game figure, knight instead of pawn

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the chess word

parts.note: a piece is a playing figure in chess
P is chess notation for pawn
N is chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A family member plays chess and swaps a pawn for a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instead of' replaces P in PIECE with N.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family relation.

clue.text: Opportunist close to clay court

parts.note: a chancer is an opportunist who takes risks

indicators.note: close here is the end, so the last letter of clay

explanation.surface: A risk-taking tennis player approaches a clay court.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancery is a division of the English High Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is historically the Lord Chancellor's court, now a High Court division.

clue.text: Division of British farm that's large

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm, typically for cattle

explanation.surface: Part of a big farm in Britain is split off as its own unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a subdivision of an organisation, like a local office of a bank.

clue.text: Everyone in base (except Tom) gets vote

indicators.note: the word for everyone sits in the shortened base
the name Tom is excluded from the synonym for base

parts.note: the bottom is the base of something
taken as the letters of the name
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone at the base apart from one man takes part in a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except Tom' cuts BOTTOM to BOT; ALL goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is a secret vote.

clue.text: This vicar, poor keeper of records

indicators.note: poor suggests the words are in a bad way, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman is criticised for badly maintaining parish records.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist curates documents and historical files.

clue.text: Swindled head of company, furious

indicators.note: only the first letter, the head, of company is taken

parts.note: heated means angry or furious

explanation.surface: A conned employee rails at the company boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cheated is to be defrauded or conned.

clue.text: The one in possession is alert

definitions.meaning: in football, the player in possession literally has the ball at their feet

explanation.surface: A footballer with the ball has to be sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means quick to react, while literally the possessor stands with a foot on the football.

clue.text: Stuff round end of profiterole?

indicators.note: the synonym for stuff goes around the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to cram is to stuff full

indicators.note: only the final letter of profiterole is taken

explanation.surface: A question about what fills the pastry around a choux bun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts E, the last letter of profiterole, inside CRAM; the whole clue also describes the filling of a profiterole.
explanation.definitionFit: Profiteroles are choux buns filled with whipped dairy filling, the stuffing inside the pastry.

clue.text: Penitent from Ely anagrammed incorrectly

indicators.note: the words are set out incorrectly, so their letters need putting in a new order

explanation.surface: A repentant sinner from a cathedral city has their name jumbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagrammed' is fodder, not the signal; the signal is 'incorrectly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical follower of Jesus is traditionally portrayed as a repentant sinner.

clue.text: Leader in theatre seen struggling under pressure

indicators.note: the leading, first letter of theatre is taken
the word seen is struggling, so its letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre's star performer is seen floundering under stress.
explanation.walkthrough: T leads; 'struggling' turns SEEN into ENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense means being nervous and strained, as when under stress.

clue.text: Singer in church, or nun needing no introduction

indicators.note: the first letter, the introduction, is dropped from the word for nun

parts.note: a nun is called Sister

explanation.surface: A church singer is compared with a nun of great renown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' drops the first letter of the word for nun; 'in' is just a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a choir, especially a church choir.

clue.text: Ship's hands initially wearing new anoraks

indicators.note: the rearranged coat letters are worn around the single letter, enclosing it
a new version of anoraks is a rearrangement of its letters
only the first letter of hands is used

explanation.surface: A ship's crew members sport fresh waterproof jackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ANORAKS; 'wearing' puts H (from 'hands initially') inside. 'Ship's' is 'Ship is', so the definition is 'Ship'.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical vessel built to survive the Flood is the most famous ship of legend.

clue.text: Shabbily-dressed person shows, at first, concern about string

indicators.note: only the first letter of shows is taken

parts.note: care means concern
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a row is a string or line of things

explanation.surface: A tramp looks worried about some twine.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a ragged, untidy person is likened to a straw figure in a field.

clue.text: A crown duke, one made out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word made is out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duke's coronet is identified by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MADE to ADEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a jewelled headband or circlet worn as a symbol of royalty.

clue.text: Greatly upsets small milliners

parts.note: milliners make hats, so they are hatters

explanation.surface: Petty hat-makers cause great distress.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter someone is to devastate them emotionally.

clue.text: A song and dance, notice

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
an ad is an advertisement or notice

explanation.surface: An advert promoting a musical number with dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'song and dance' looks like the phrase for a fuss; 'and' just joins dance to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song, often sentimental.

clue.text: Hunting dog and horse put through awfully cruel runs

indicators.note: the drug goes through the middle of the other letters
cruel treated awfully gets its letters jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A hound and a horse are driven through a harsh course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns CRUEL into LURCE; with R, 'put through' inserts H.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred sighthound used for hunting rabbits and hares.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink got cheap abroad

indicators.note: abroad means astray or widely scattered, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone picks up inexpensive booze on a trip overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: A chota peg is Anglo-Indian for a small measure of whisky, which suits 'abroad'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Raj slang a chota peg is a small whisky, usually with soda.

clue.text: Cut cut and cut a vegetable

indicators.note: the second cut means the synonym for the first is itself cut short

parts.note: to pare is to cut
to snip is to cut

explanation.surface: A cook chops and chops and chops a root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' (the second) trims PARE to PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root crop related to the carrot.

clue.text: Watch fire in northern half of Bucks town

indicators.note: in a down clue the northern half is the top, first half of the word

parts.note: Beaconsfield is a town in Buckinghamshire, Bucks for short

explanation.surface: A night watch lights a fire in part of a Buckinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Beaconsfield is a commuter town in Buckinghamshire, an English county; its first six letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal fire lit on a hill to give warning.

clue.text: Consistency shown by soldiers during a salute

indicators.note: the soldiers come in the middle of the salute, as if it happens while they are there

parts.note: to greet is to salute
men is a common crossword word for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops show uniformity while saluting.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement is concord or consistency, as between parts of speech in grammar.

clue.text: Vessel seen in China or Taiwan

indicators.note: the letters are visible within the run of words China or Taiwan

explanation.surface: A ship spotted in one of two East Asian countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, a blood vessel.

clue.text: Stand in English river by end of weir

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: only the final letter of weir is taken

explanation.surface: A man stands in a Yorkshire river beside a weir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' is a noun: a frame for drying clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a clothes horse, a frame for drying washing.

clue.text: Number three, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the letters of three

explanation.surface: A question about which figure comes third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is something that numbs, not a figure: an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Diethyl ether was an early anaesthetic, a substance that numbs.

clue.text: The thumbs up for demolition

definitions.meaning: the knocking down of buildings, as in slum work

explanation.surface: Permission is granted to knock a building down.
explanation.definitionFit: It means authorisation, and also the removal of buildings, as in slum work.

clue.text: Doctor with a secure contract

parts.note: to win something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A physician signs a deal for a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun at the end of the surface; it is a verb, to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw in is to shrink or close up, as days do in autumn.

clue.text: Tricky situation to contain one animal disease

indicators.note: the word for a fix holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: a scrape is a predicament
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A predicament involving a sick animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal brain disorder of sheep and goats.
